why: B: on every abstract connected Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with any smooth Mathlib RiemannianBundle metric and any Levi-Civita connection (Milnor's axioms), if ⟨R(A,B)A,B⟩ ≤ 0 for all A, B (Milnor's sign, IsCurvVal) then no a, b ∈ [0,1] are conjugate along any geodesic γ : [0,1] → M (no completeness). A (universes 0): for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric only: NonposCurvature ⇔ all sectional curvatures ≤ 0; the derivative formula d/dt⟨DJ/dt,J⟩ = ‖DJ/dt‖² − ⟨R(V,J)V,J⟩; the key step (a Jacobi field vanishing at a < b vanishes on [0,1]); Lemma 19.1. A ⇒ B fails genuinely (abstract manifolds are not given embedded; the project has no abstract Jacobi/curvature theory); B ⇒ A fails genuinely (setting, and A's sectional-curvature equivalence and derivative formula are not consequences of B). On embedded manifolds the core claims coincide (proved both ways, see the embedded note).
overlap: No A_to_B/B_to_A. For the embedded theorem B_emb_to_A_geo: 175 shared project theorems — tangent-projection / second-fundamental-form / curvOp lemmas (curvOp_mem, curvR_of_mem, tanProj_*, dN_*), slice-chart and Gram-projection lemmas, IsSmoothCurveIn/IsJacobiField basics, all reached through RoundTrip/Bridge.lean (isCurvVal_iff, hasCovDeriv_iff') and the Jacobi dictionary; none of the argument of Lemma 19.1 (hasDerivAt_inner_covAlong, the monotonicity of ⟨DJ/dt, J⟩, IsJacobiField.eqOn_zero) is shared.
